newsitem.title: USA: Bond lawyers "disappointed" by IRS ruling.
newsitem.headline: Bond lawyers "disappointed" by IRS ruling.

text.p: Municipal bond lawyers meeting here on Wednesday for an annual conference said they were unhappy with the Internal Revenue Service's announcement this morning on "yield burning."
IRS said in a five-page notice it will give municipalities that overpaid their underwriters for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market more time to reach closing agreements with the Service.
And the Service also requested detailed comments on the controversial ruling it issued in July setting up the closing agreement procedure.
But to the dismay of bond market participants, it refused to suspend the ruling while reviewing its contents.

"I'm not happy about it," David Walton, a former IRS official who is now an attorney with Jones Hill & White in San Francisco, said in an interview with Reuters at the National Association of Bond Lawyers annual workshop.

"They know this is a real serious problem. This isn't just a few bad eggs. This potentially applies to everybody for the last 25 years that issued advance refunding bonds and bought over market," Walton said.

Mitchell Rapaport, an attorney with Nixon, Hargrave, Devans & Doyle in Washington, said, "I'm disappointed because they left the revenue procedure in place for now. I thought they would suspend it for now until they get comment."

Another prominent bond lawyer attending the conference said, "We are disappointed they didn't suspend it. But they cedrtainly have sought comment from us on the substantial provisions," he said. "I'm sure we will give them to them."
